message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **long‑weekend** periods that Canadians can enjoy in 2023, based on the federal holidays that fall on or near weekends. (Note that some holidays are province‑specific; the list below focuses on the nationwide public holidays that create extended weekends.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Weekend Days Included | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------|-------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Sunday, Jan 1 | Sat Dec 30 – Mon Jan 3 | Observed on Monday, Jan 2 |
| **Victoria Day** | Monday, May 22 | Sat May 20 – Mon May 22 | National holiday |
| **Canada Day** | Saturday, July 1 | Sat July 1 – Mon July 3 | Observed on Monday, July 3 |
| **Labour Day** | Monday, Sept 4 | Sat Sept 2 – Mon Sept 4 | National holiday |
| **Thanksgiving** | Monday, Oct 9 | Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9 | National holiday |
| **Christmas** | Monday, Dec 25 | Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25 | National holiday |

### Quick Summary

- **January 1–3** (New Year’s Day)  
- **May 20–22** (Victoria Day)  
- **July 1–3** (Canada Day)  
- **Sept 2–4** (Labour Day)  
- **Oct 7–9** (Thanksgiving)  
- **Dec 23–25** (Christmas)

These are the most common long‑weekend stretches that Canadians can plan around in 2023. If you’re targeting a specific province, you’ll want to add any provincial holidays that fall on a weekday and are observed on the following Monday (e.g., Family Day in Ontario, British Columbia, etc.).
